question: Can a class-balanced gradient-boosting classifier on windowed thread-state features separate true livelocks from long legitimate waits better than a standard no-progress timeout detector?
method: Synthetic thread wait traces; stratified 75/25 split (seed 42); baseline = max-gap no-progress timeout with window tuned on train; improved = class-balanced LightGBM on windowed features with CV-tuned hyperparameters and OOF-tuned threshold; test set used once.
baseline: No-progress timeout: flag a thread if no shared-state write occurs within a window of 60 steps (window tuned on train).
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM on windowed features (state-repeat counts, time since last shared write, wait length, distinct-state ratio, etc.) with CV-tuned hyperparameters and threshold.
notes: Synthetic traces with hand-designed generative assumptions, not the paper's programs or logs; results depend on those assumptions. The baseline is deterministic, so its seed runs are identical (std 0). Only the LightGBM model varies with seed; the CV folds and threshold use seed 42. Single split, so differences are indicative rather than statistically established.
